title: Terraform module for VPC egress routing, subnet orchestration, and service endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a reusable Terraform module that standardizes VPC networking for Redwood Private deployments focused on egress routing patterns, subnet allocation across AZs, and creation/management of AWS VPC Gateway and Interface Endpoints. The module must support hub-and-spoke and single-VPC topologies, provide clear upgrade paths for existing stacks, and include automated health checks and drift detection hooks.

Scope and responsibilities:
- Provision VPC with configurable CIDR blocks and multi-AZ subnet allocation (control/data/egress) using a deterministic allocator to avoid overlapping CIDRs with peered networks. Support explicit IPAM-friendly inputs.
- Create and manage Internet Gateway (IGW) and an option for centralized NAT Gateway(s) or per-subnet NATs. Allow configuration for: NAT Gateway (recommended), NAT Instances (legacy), and centralized egress via a shared NAT account.
- Add route tables per subnet type with explicit routes for private subnets to NAT, public subnets to IGW, and egress-only IGW for IPv6 when enabled. Support route table tagging and route propagation control for Direct Connect/VPN attachments.
- Create recommended VPC endpoints: S3 (Gateway), ECR API and ECR DKR (Interface), SSM, EC2messages, CloudWatch Logs, STS, and optional KMS. Provide variable-driven enable/disable for each endpoint and endpoint policy insertion point so customers can attach least-privilege policies.
- Provide output variables for core identifiers (vpc_id, subnet_ids by type, nat_gateway_ids, route_table_ids, endpoint_ids) and a stable module versioning strategy.
- Integrate health checks: a lightweight Terraform null_resource that runs AWS CLI/SDK validation post-apply (examples: verify NAT Gateway elastic IP association, endpoint ENI active, route exists). Also emit metrics to our observability pipeline via an ephemeral CloudWatch metric or a webhook for the console to surface immediate infra health post-deployment.
- Include upgrade/migration tooling notes: when changing subnet sizing or enabling/disabling endpoints the module must surface an explicit plan and recommended mitigation steps (backup state, use import for existing resources, use route table replacement strategy to avoid transient blackholes).
- Provide a policy/guardrail layer: optional IAM role used by terraform with least privilege S3 endpoint policy example, and a checklist for security review.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- NAT Gateway vs. NAT Instances: NAT Gateway is recommended for reliability and low ops burden; support NAT Instances only for customers with extreme cost sensitivity or specialized routing needs. Document cost implications and provide a toggle.
- Centralized egress (single NAT in a shared account) is supported but requires cross-account route management; include examples but mark as advanced configuration.
- Interface Endpoints (ENIs) will increase ENI counts in AZs; add a safeguard variable that prevents creating more than X endpoints per AZ and surfaces guidance for customers on ENI limits.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to mark Done):
- Module is published to our Terraform registry with semantic versioning and clear upgrade notes.
- Automated unit/integration tests: terraform validate, terratest or kitchen-terraform suite that verifies: VPC and subnets created across requested AZs, route tables contain expected routes, NAT Gateway reachable for private subnets, S3 gateway endpoint usable from a private subnet, interface endpoints show active ENIs.
- Post-apply health checks run automatically and surface failures as warnings.
- PR reviewed by infra owner and security; documentation in the private-deploy runbook plus example usage snippet added to the Private Deployments Confluence page.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Module scaffolding and variables/outputs spec (Aisha).
- Core VPC, subnets, IGW, route table resources (Marco).
- NAT Gateway options + cost guidance and centralization patterns (Marco).
- Endpoint resources with toggles and policies (Aisha).
- Health check null_resources and observability hooks (Marco + SRE).
- Terratest suite + CI job (CI owner).
- Docs, runbook, and upgrade migration guide (Aisha).

Rollback and upgrade notes:
- Changing subnet CIDR sizes or moving subnets between route tables can cause service disruption. The module must default to non-destructive changes and fail the plan if an action will replace a subnet resource. Provide documented manual steps (snapshot state, import, create new subnets and migrate ENIs) for unavoidable changes.
- For enabling/disabling endpoints, the module will prefer in-place modifications. If an endpoint needs replacement, run the health checks to validate connectivity immediately and provide rollback commands in the module output.

Observability and SLOs:
- Add CloudWatch metrics for: endpoint creation failures, NAT gateway elastic IP dissociation, route table drift detected by periodic terraform plan job.
- Expose token-bucket-style throttling metadata for endpoints in the console guidance to help customers estimate API limits for interface endpoints.

Security and compliance:
- Module will include example KMS policy patterns where endpoints require encryption.
- Endpoint policy insertion points will be documented with recommended least-privilege templates.
- Because this module touches routing and egress, mark security_review_required=true and schedule a brief design review with security and network teams before merge.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module published under modules/rdw/vpc-networking-egress (registry artifact).
- Integration test pipeline job in CI that deploys into a sandbox account and runs the health checks.
- Upgrade guide and runbook in Confluence with explicit migration commands.
- PR with code and example composition for a Private deployment template.

Notes and open questions:
- Should we include managed NAT gateway autoscaling (multiple NATs with route table weight-based failover) or keep initial offering simple? Recommendation: ship simple first, follow-up epic to add multi-NAT resilience.
- Cross-account centralized NAT patterns need more security review (route propagation and shared EIPs).
